title: Pesticide Exposure at Work May Increase Motor Neurone Disease Risk
author: Rachel Tan
text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementHealthPesticide Exposure at Work May Increase Motor Neurone Disease RiskA new review looked at 1,734 people with ALS. But it couldn’t separate pesticide from other risk factors, such as head trauma.RTBy Rachel Tan9:00 AM CDT on August 7, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleBeing diagnosed with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), also known as Lou Gehrig’s disease, can be devastating.Subscribe to skip adsFeatured VideoPowered By 10 Almost 20% of Earth’s Mammal Species Could Be Undiscovered!ShareNextStayALS is the most common form of motor neurone disease, a neurodegenerative condition that affects people’s ability to speak, eat, breathe, and swallow. It is debilitating and progresses rapidly: on average, people survive just 2 to 3 years after a diagnosis. Most people are diagnosed between the ages of 40 and 70.A new study, published earlier this week, has found that being exposed to pesticide at work can increase the risk of developing ALS by 61 to 71 percent. The study brings together the findings of eight other studies—but not all of them assess risk in the same way. Here’s why we need to interpret the findings with caution.Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
